apparatus_caveat: The witnesses are mediated by the 1896 editorial collection. Modern Basil and Chrysostom derive from the source-described Venice 1869 text; Greek James is attributed to Paris gr. 2509, with its stated date corrected to the fifteenth century in the edition’s corrigenda. Source typography marks scriptural quotations, and speech-block/rubric normalization is explicitly recorded. No Catholic reception, original composition date or date of textual introduction follows from this comparison. Brightman p. 406 footnote a separately characterizes Μεταβαλὼν τῷ Πνεύματί σου τῷ Ἁγίῳ as wording copied from Chrysostom into Basil, which it treats as an addition by an unnamed person and syntactically inappropriate there; it refers to Nicodemus’s Pedalion note on canon 19 of Laodicea. That apparatus wording is not in Brightman’s printed Basil prayer, whereas the clause is in his Chrysostom prayer at p. 387. The note identifies no receiving edition or introduction date; the cited Pedalion itself was not inspected, and this editorial testimony is not converted into a directed book relationship.
basis: The complete bounded priestly invocation over the gifts in the Basil and Chrysostom liturgies, as actually printed in Brightman 1896. The original Greek texts were independently checked against the exact retained pages. The paired liturgical functions and explicit prayer boundaries establish comparison membership; shared wording and variants do not establish borrowing direction or a common ancestor.
